福爾摩沙小導遊臺南 Tainan・中西區

林百貨Hayashi Department Store

認識臺南銀座上的摩登五棧樓：南臺灣第一部流籠、屋頂神社、戰爭彈痕，以及它如何變成文創百貨。

Meet the modern five-story store on Tainan's Ginza: its elevator, rooftop shrine, war scars and new life.

中正路熱鬧的街角，有一棟五層樓的百貨，走過繁華、戰火和沉寂。1932 年 12 月，它在有「臺南銀座」之稱的末廣町開幕；可惜創辦人林方一五天後就病逝了。人們排隊搭南臺灣第一部電梯「流籠」，指針刻度盤至今仍指著每一層樓。屋頂上有一座小神社。1945 年美軍飛機掃射，彈痕到今天還在。戰後製鹽總廠、糧食局和空軍電臺進駐，後來大樓空置了許多年。1998 年列為古蹟，經過修復，2014 年 6 月以文創百貨重新開幕。

On a busy corner of Zhongzheng Road stands a five-story store that has lived through boom times, war and silence. It opened in December 1932 on Suehiro-cho, the Ginza of Tainan. Sadly, its founder, Mr. Hayashi, died just five days later. Shoppers lined up to ride southern Taiwan's first elevator, the liu-long. A pointer on a dial still shows each floor. Up on the roof sits a small Shinto shrine. In 1945, American planes strafed the building, and the bullet marks are still there. After the war, the salt works, the Food Bureau and an Air Force radio station moved in. Then the building stood empty for years. Named a heritage site in 1998 and carefully restored, it reopened in June 2014 as a cultural and creative department store.

一分鐘看懂

One-minute intro

為什麼值得來

Why it matters & history

林百貨是臺灣日治時期兩大百貨之一，有南臺灣第一部電梯，屋頂還有神社。它走過繁華、空襲和空置，修復後重新開幕，是臺南最有代表性的老建築再利用。

Hayashi was one of the two great department stores of the Japanese era. It had southern Taiwan's first elevator and a shrine on its roof. It lived through boom years, air raids and decades of silence, and its restoration is one of Tainan's best-known second lives for an old building.

  1. 193212 月 5 日在末廣町開幕，創辦人林方一五天後病逝。Opens on 5 December; the founder, Hayashi Hoichi, dies five days later.
  2. 1933屋頂設立末廣社。The rooftop shrine is set up.
  3. 1945美軍空襲掃射，屋頂留下彈痕。Allied air raids leave bullet marks on the roof.
  4. 戰後 After 1945製鹽總廠、糧食局、空軍電臺等單位進駐，之後空置多年。Government offices move in; later the building stands empty for years.
  5. 1998列為古蹟。Listed as a historic site.
  6. 2014修復完成，6 月重新開幕。Reopens in June after restoration.

認識景點

About the place

開幕與創辦人Opening day and the founder

從山口縣來的商人：林方一出生於日本山口縣，1912 年來到臺南，從小商店做起。 臺灣第二家百貨：只比臺北菊元百貨晚幾天開幕，兩家並稱日治時期的南北大百貨。 開幕五天後病逝：林方一在開幕前病倒，1932 年 12 月 10 日病逝臺北，沒能看著百貨長大；妻子接手經營。 一層一種商品：一樓化妝品與糖果、三樓布料服飾、四樓文具玩具，五樓是餐廳咖啡。

A merchant from Yamaguchi: Mr. Hayashi came from Yamaguchi in Japan and started a small shop in Tainan in 1912. Taiwan's second department store: It opened just days after Kikumoto in Taipei. The two were the big stores of the north and the south. Gone in five days: Mr. Hayashi fell ill before the opening and died in Taipei on December 10, 1932. His wife kept the store running. A floor for everything: Cosmetics and sweets were downstairs, clothes and toys above, and a restaurant on the fifth floor.

臺南銀座：末廣町是 1932 年完工的新商店街，路寬燈亮，人稱「臺南銀座」。

The Ginza of Tainan: Suehiro-cho was a brand-new shopping street, so bright and modern that people called it the Ginza of Tainan.

摩登五棧樓A modern five-story building

流籠：南臺灣第一部電梯，臺語叫「流籠」；搭流籠是當年最時髦的事。 指針式樓層盤：電梯門上的刻度盤用指針顯示樓層，十足復古。 從 12 人到 6 人：電梯原本可載 12 人；修復時為了保留原本的電梯井，改成 6 人座。 轉角圓窗：轉角二到五樓是圓窗；女兒牆在轉角最高，往兩側逐段降低。

liu-long, the elevator: Southern Taiwan's first elevator was called liu-long. Riding it was the latest fashion. The pointer dial: Above the elevator door, a dial with a pointer shows the floor. From twelve riders to six: The car once held twelve people. To keep the original shaft, the new car holds six. Round corner windows: Round windows climb the corner, and the parapet steps down on both sides.

裝飾藝術：外牆貼溝面磚，騎樓柱有裝飾紋樣，室內柱子是裝飾藝術風格。 手搖鐵捲門與沖水馬桶：當年還有手搖鐵捲門、避雷針和沖水馬桶，全是摩登設備。

Art Deco: Grooved tiles cover the walls, and the columns inside are Art Deco. Shutters and flush toilets: Hand-cranked steel shutters and flush toilets were modern wonders too.

屋頂神社與戰火The rooftop shrine and the war

末廣社：開幕約半年後的 1933 年設立，是守護會社的神社，當年不對顧客開放。 平直的鳥居：修復時請日本的林家後代協助，確認鳥居上橫樑原本是平直的。 1945 年空襲：二戰末期屋頂設了機槍陣地；美軍轟炸、掃射，大樓受損卻沒有倒。 保留的彈痕：屋頂上的彈痕被刻意保留下來，讓後人記得戰爭。

Suehiro Shrine: Set up in 1933, this small Shinto shrine protected the business. Shoppers could not visit it then. A straight top beam: The Hayashi family in Japan helped confirm that the torii's top beam was straight. The 1945 air raids: Near the end of the war, machine guns stood on the roof. American planes bombed and strafed the store, but it stood. Bullet marks kept: The bullet marks on the roof were kept so that people remember the war.

戰後的新住客：戰後由政府接收：製鹽總廠用一到三樓、糧食局用四樓、空軍電臺用五、六樓；後來還有鹽警、保警與眷舍，之後空置多年。

New tenants after the war: After the war, the salt works, the Food Bureau and an Air Force radio station moved in. Later the police used it, and then it stood empty for years.

實景照片

Photos on site

五層樓的轉角 The five-story corner

林百貨 1932 年開幕，是當時臺南最高的建築之一，被叫做「五棧樓仔」。轉角處像塔一樣往上收，頂端是階梯狀的山牆，正中間嵌著林百貨的「林」字標誌；一排排圓形的小窗，是裝飾藝術（Art Deco）風格的特色。

Hayashi opened in 1932 and was one of the tallest buildings in Tainan, nicknamed the five-story building. The corner rises like a tower to a stepped top with the store's emblem in the middle. The round windows are typical of the Art Deco style.

黃昏的正面 The front at dusk

黃昏時，土黃色的溝面磚牆被夕陽照得暖暖的。二樓陽台中間掛著圓形的「林」字商標，四、五樓的窗戶做成弧形的陽台，一樓的騎樓下就是百貨的入口。

At sunset, the yellow-brown tiled walls glow warmly. The round store emblem hangs on the second-floor balcony, the upper floors have curved balconies, and the shop entrances sit under the arcade on the ground floor.

夜晚的林百貨 Hayashi at night

晚上整棟樓打上燈，屋頂邊緣一排小燈，像在提醒大家：這裡曾是臺南最摩登的地方。百貨營業到晚上，可以逛完晚餐再來。

At night the whole building lights up, with a row of small lamps along the roof. The store stays open into the evening, so you can come after dinner.

夜晚的轉角 The corner at night

從中正路和忠義路口看過去，燈光照亮轉角塔上的圓窗和陽台，招牌寫著 DEP'T-STORE HAYASHI。這個路口在日治時期是熱鬧的「末廣町」，被稱作臺南銀座。

From the crossroads, lights pick out the round windows and balconies on the corner tower. In the Japanese era this busy street was called the Ginza of Tainan.

溝面磚 Scratch tiles

林百貨的外牆貼滿一條一條刻著溝紋的「溝面磚」，日文叫「スクラッチタイル」(scratch tile)，是日治時期建築常用的面磚。據說這種有溝紋的土黃色面磚可以減少反光，戰時也比較不顯眼。

The outside walls are covered with grooved tiles called scratch tiles. Many buildings in the Japanese era used them. It is said the grooves cut down glare and made the building harder to spot in wartime.

流籠的樓層指針 The elevator's floor dial

林百貨有南臺灣第一部電梯，當年大家叫它「流籠」。電梯門上方有一個扇形刻度盤，上面有 I 到 V 五個數字，指針會轉到電梯所在的樓層。

Hayashi had southern Taiwan's first elevator. People called it liu-long. Above the door, a fan-shaped dial shows the numbers one to five, and a pointer swings to the floor the elevator is on.

屋頂的彈孔 Bullet holes on the roof

頂樓這面牆上的坑洞和破損，是 1945 年二戰末期美軍飛機空襲、用機槍掃射留下的痕跡。現在牆前裝了玻璃保護，讓大家記得戰爭。

The holes and damage on this rooftop wall come from the 1945 air raids near the end of World War Two, when American planes shot at the building from the air. Today a glass screen protects the wall, so people remember the war.

末廣社遺跡 Remains of Suehiro Shrine

頂樓的末廣社在 1933 年設立。現在還看得到石鳥居、兩座石燈籠和神社的石基座；鳥居最上面的橫樑是平直的。後面就是臺南市區的高樓。

Suehiro Shrine was set up on the roof in 1933. Today you can still see a stone torii gate, two stone lanterns and the shrine's stone base. The torii's top beam is straight. Behind them is the Tainan skyline.

老地圖文具 Old-map stationery

林百貨裡賣的不只是衣服和食品，還有許多臺灣設計的文創商品。這區的筆記本和資料夾印著日治昭和年間的老地圖，可以找找看「臺南市」和「臺南市全圖」，對照今天走過的街道。

Hayashi sells more than clothes and food. It is full of gifts designed in Taiwan. These notebooks and folders are printed with old maps from the 1930s. Look for the maps of Tainan and compare them with the streets you walked today.

剪紙杯墊 Paper-cut coasters

紅色的圓形杯墊做成傳統剪紙的樣子，上面剪出「福」字、花草和吉祥圖案，是很受歡迎的伴手禮。

These round red coasters look like traditional Chinese paper cuts, with the word for luck, flowers and other lucky patterns. They make popular gifts.

像真的一樣的魚和菜 Fish and veggies that are not food

竹篩上的紅魚、斑點魚和高麗菜看起來像剛從市場買回來，其實是布做的抱枕和收納包，有的還做成魚頭零錢包，讓人忍不住笑出來。

The red fish, spotted fish and cabbages on these bamboo trays look fresh from the market, but they are cloth cushions and pouches. Some are even coin purses shaped like fish heads.

藍染圍巾 Indigo-dyed scarves

一排深淺不同的藍染圍巾，有漸層、條紋和像雲一樣的紮染花紋。藍染是用植物染料一次次浸泡染成的，每一條的顏色都不太一樣。

A row of indigo-dyed scarves shows fades, stripes and cloud-like tie-dye patterns. Indigo comes from plants, and the cloth is dipped again and again, so no two scarves are quite the same.

林百貨紙鎮 Hayashi paperweights

一顆顆圓圓的陶瓷紙鎮，中間都壓著林百貨的「林」字標誌，有綠、粉、紫各種釉色，是手工限量製作的紀念品。

These round ceramic paperweights each carry the Hayashi logo in the middle, in green, pink and purple glazes. They are handmade in small batches as souvenirs.

壽桃與囍字陶器 Peach and double-happiness pots

桌上的白瓷小罐做成包子的樣子，放在竹蒸籠裡；粉紅的是祝壽用的壽桃，前排圓盒蓋上印著「囍」字，是婚禮常見的吉祥字。

These little white pots look like steamed buns sitting in a bamboo steamer. The pink ones are shaped like birthday peaches, and the round boxes in front carry the double-happiness sign used at weddings.

紅紙包的祝福 Wrapped good wishes

牛皮紙包外面貼著大紅紙，寫著「福」「順」「好」「珍」等吉祥字，再用麻繩綁起來，像老式柑仔店的包裝。

These brown paper packs are wrapped with red paper printed with lucky words such as fortune and smooth sailing, then tied with string, like goods from an old corner shop.
